assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED showed that a superconducting artificial atom can be strongly and controllably coupled to a single microwave photon in an on-chip resonator, opening a new regime of light-matter interaction and supplying the dispersive-readout, coupling and gate toolbox on which present superconducting processors rest. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits; cQED is the complementary and equally foundational step that made those circuits controllable quantum systems. Conceptually clean and reproduced in many laboratories.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff et al. (Nature 2004) gave the first strong-coupling experiment in the Schoelkopf group at Yale. A fair split is the two experimental leaders plus the theorist Blais, but Steven Girvin (not in the supplied credit) was a co-author of the proposal, so allocation is not fully clean. As a close colleague of this community I note a possible conflict of interest and rely on the physics case.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of confirmation across many groups and platforms (transmon, readout, bosonic codes, hybrid systems). Interpretation is stable and the discovery is fully mature, and the 2025 prize does not subsume it.
uncertainties: Credited names omit Girvin and others who co-authored the original proposal, so a three-person split leaves an unresolved credit question.
Possible overlap with the 2025 prize may lead colleagues to see the field as already honoured.
My proximity to the field may bias my judgement upward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal turned trapped ions into a concrete quantum-gate architecture, and the same authors' later work on cold-atom quantum simulation and quantum optics shaped a whole experimental programme. It is a conceptual foundation of quantum information processing with atoms, and it complements the 2012 prize for measuring and manipulating single quantum systems.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is the natural and widely recognised duo with no obvious competing theorists in the supplied list. Experimental realisation is attributed to others (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe), who are not part of this candidate, which keeps the prize theory-led and clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature: ion gates, quantum simulators and Rydberg platforms follow directly from the proposals, and fault-tolerant demonstrations keep building on them. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to pair theory with trapped-ion experimentalists, which would change the configuration.
Considerable overlap with other candidates carrying Cirac and Zoller (B024, B029) means the discovery should be defined narrowly.
The prize rewards the discovery, and the application to computing is still far from fault tolerance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall proposal and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction, confirmed by Molenkamp's group, opened a new class of topological band insulators with protected edge states. It is a clear case of a new regime of matter, theory and experiment closing the loop. Impact reaches spintronics, topological superconductivity and quantum-computing proposals.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the graphene-based Z2 proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive HgTe observation. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction and Zhang's role are left out of the supplied credit, which is a real allocation problem. The three-person group is defensible only if the committee accepts that framing.
assessment.maturity: Observed in several materials by independent groups (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3 via ARPES). Mature, but the 2016 prize on topological phases may make the committee reluctant to return to the area.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the credited names.
Possible overlap with B012 and the 2016 prize.
The graphene case of Kane-Mele is not experimentally realised at the predicted gap size.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle, created the moire quantum-materials field with tunable strongly correlated physics. It is a new regime that is reproduced widely and has spawned many follow-on discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Theoretical prediction by Bistritzer and MacDonald; decisive experiments by Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (including Cao, the lead author, who is not credited). The credited three form a plausible configuration, but the student-led nature of the experiment and other theorists complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many laboratories since 2018 and quickly mature, though the interpretation of superconductivity and correlated states is not settled.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain debated.
Sample-dependence and reproducibility details across devices.
Impact may still be early compared with older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength idea, enables clock stability and accuracy at the 10^-18 level, pushing precision measurement, tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. A clean, concrete invention with clear lasting importance. It belongs to measurement rather than quantum-circuit physics, where my expertise is lighter, so I defer in part to colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group made decisive strontium clock realisations and the frequency-comb link. Other contributors (Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for combs) are not part of the credit. A two-person prize looks fair.
assessment.maturity: Several independent clocks across the world agree at the 10^-18 level, and redefinition of the second is under discussion, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Competing credit for trapped-ion clocks and other lattice work.
Some Nobel emphasis would be on application rather than discovery.
My limited expertise in precision metrology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bringing mechanical oscillators to their quantum ground state and showing entanglement and squeezing opened macroscopic quantum mechanics to controlled experiments. Cleland's work with a superconducting qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator and to surface acoustic waves is a close relative of circuit quantum acoustodynamics, which I know well and which our own group has also contributed to.
assessment.attribution: The ground-state cooling and quantum-control demonstrations are spread among several groups (O'Connell and Cleland, Teufel and Lehnert, Chan and Painter, Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg). The three-name split omits Lehnert, Teufel, Painter and Schwab, so attribution is the weakest part of this candidate.
assessment.maturity: The field is well confirmed but still evolving and has few applications yet, so recognition would be somewhat early compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Dispersed credit across many groups makes a three-person prize hard to justify.
Whether the discovery is one result or a cluster of results.
My own links to circuit-acoustic work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson was a milestone experiment that completed the Standard Model and verified the mechanism recognised in 2013. Its scientific importance is beyond doubt. As the experiment is outside my field, I defer to the particle physicists on the committee.
assessment.attribution: The experiments are very large collaborations, and the prize rules limit awards to three persons. The three credited names are the founding spokespersons or initiators and can be seen as representing the collaborations, but their individual discoveries are not obvious and the allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed with several independent decay channels, though the Higgs couplings are still being measured precisely.
uncertainties: The collaboration structure makes fair attribution to individuals problematic.
Whether the prize would be awarded for leadership rather than discovery.
I lack particle-physics depth.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes and fault tolerance underpin all scalable quantum computing and are essential for the programme I help lead. The 1995-96 papers showed that errors can be corrected without violating quantum mechanics, a conceptual breakthrough. Honouring them now might feel timely given the experimental progress below threshold.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane devised the first codes, Calderbank and Shor and Steane the CSS construction, and Kitaev the topological codes and fault tolerance; Knill, Laflamme, Gottesman, Preskill and others contributed decisively and are not credited. Attribution is therefore difficult.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical qubits are recent, so full impact is not yet in place, which makes this candidate somewhat premature. The discovery is a theoretical one and the technology is still ahead of us.
uncertainties: Many decisive contributors are missing from the credit list.
Whether the committee views it as physics rather than computer science or mathematics.
Large-scale fault-tolerant computing has not yet been shown.
